page: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a 472 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. The underlying virtualization is managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the D8ds_v7 demonstrates solid mid-tier performance across most compute and memory metrics. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng fall within the average range, with scores of 2277.87 and 9302.94 respectively. However, the processor exhibits strong single-threaded performance in data compression and decompression tasks, with gzip compression reaching 35.05 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 15.08 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is measured at 687.52 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 89.09 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the instance achieves a strong text generation speed of 270.06 tokens/sec using a small 135M parameter LLM model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8ds_v7 offers a balanced resource density suitable for mainstream enterprise workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory or compute-heavy instances. The inclusion of a 472 GB local disk and Premium Storage capability provides a cost-effective path for workloads requiring fast local scratch space or reliable database storage. This server is well-suited for general-purpose applications, relational databases, web serving, application servers, and moderate data processing tasks such as single-threaded compression pipelines or lightweight LLM inference.
